facts.statement: Sinoceratops lived between 77.3 and 73.5 million years ago in what is now Shandong province, China.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived from 77.3 to 73.5 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Shandong province in China.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2010 by Xu Xing and colleagues based on three skulls found in Zhucheng, China.
facts.quote: It was named in 2010 by Xu Xing et al. for three skulls from Zhucheng, China.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops was a medium-sized, quadrupedal herbivore that lived on the ground.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops was a medium-sized, averagely-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops was the first ceratopsid discovered in China and remains the only ceratopsid known from Asia.
facts.quote: It was the first ceratopsid dinosaur discovered in China, and the only ceratopsid known from Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sinoceratops were found in the Hongtuya Formation, a geological unit deposited during the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: This genus was discovered in the Hongtuya Formation (a unit of the Wangshi Group) which was deposited during the late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops could reach an estimated length of 5 meters and a weight of 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: It could grow up to an estimated 5 m in length and weigh up to 2 tonne.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, a partial skull including a braincase, was recovered in the summer of 2008 from the Hongtuya Formation in Shandong, China.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen ZCDM V0010, consisting of a partial skull, including a braincase, was in the summer of 2008 recovered at the Hongtuya Formation of the Wangshi Group in Shandong, China.

facts.statement: The name Sinoceratops means "Chinese horned face," derived from Latin and Greek roots referring to China, horn, and face.
facts.quote: The genus name Sinoceratops means "Chinese horned face", and is derived from the word Sino- referring to China from Latin Sina, the country of its discovery, and the Greek words keras (κέρας) meaning "horn", and ops (ωψ) meaning "face".

facts.statement: Sinoceratops had a short, hooked nasal horn, lacked brow horns, and possessed a short frill with forward-curving hornlets that created a crown-like appearance.
facts.quote: It has a short, hooked horn on its nose (called a nasal horn), no horns above its eyes (brow horns), and a short neck frill with a series of forward-curving hornlets that gave the frill a crown-like appearance.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops is classified as a member of the short-frilled ceratopsid subfamily, Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops is a member of the short-frilled ceratopsids, the Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: With an estimated skull length of 180 cm, Sinoceratops possesses one of the largest known centrosaurine skulls.
facts.quote: The skull of Sinoceratops is estimated to be 180 cm long making it one of the largest known centrosaurine skulls.

facts.statement: Based on skull characteristics, Sinoceratops was assigned to the taxon Centrosaurinae as a basal member.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops was assigned to the taxon Centrosaurinae, as a basal member by Xu et al. (2010) based on characteristics present in the skull.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sinoceratops represents a lineage that invaded Asia from North America, as it shares features with advanced centrosaurines not seen in primitive ones.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops however, shares a number of features with advanced centrosaurines such as Centrosaurus and Styracosaurus that are not seen in primitive centrosaurines like Diabloceratops, including a well-developed nose horn and reduced brow horns.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops lived alongside Shantungosaurus, Zhuchengtyrannus, Zhuchengceratops, and Huaxiaosaurus in the same formation.
facts.quote: Alongside it, in the formation, lived Shantungosaurus, a very common hadrosaurid to which most of the material has been assigned, Zhuchengtyrannus, an Asian tyrannosaurid related to Tarbosaurus, Zhuchengceratops, an Asian leptoceratopsid, and Huaxiaosaurus, a possible older individual of Shantungosaurus.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Sinoceratops is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Sinoceratops could grow to an estimated length of 6 meters, a height of 2 meters, and weigh up to 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Podría crecer hasta una longitud estimada de 6 metros, 2 de altura, y pesar hasta 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Sinoceratops was a large ceratopsian estimated to be about 6 meters long, 2 tons in weight, and 2 meters tall.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops era un ceratopsiano grande, con una longitud estimada de unos 6 metros, un peso de 2 toneladas y una altura de unos 2 metros.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated its length at 7 meters and its weight at 2.3 tons, comparable to a rhinoceros.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimó su longitud en 7 metros y su peso en 2,3 toneladas, el peso de un rinoceronte.

facts.statement: It possessed a short, hook-shaped nasal horn, lacked horns above the eyes or on the frill, and had a short neck frill with forward-curving horns creating a crown-like appearance.
facts.quote: Tiene un cuerno corto y en forma de gancho en la nariz, llamado cuerno nasal, sin cuernos por encima de los ojos, cuernos de la frente y un volante corto en el cuello con una serie de cuernos curvados hacia adelante que le daban una apariencia de corona.

facts.statement: A unique row of low knobs on the top of the frill, not seen in any other horned dinosaur, was located within the row of frill horns.
facts.quote: Dentro de esta fila de cuernos hay una serie de pomos bajos en la parte superior del volante, que no se ven en ningún otro dinosaurio cornudo.

facts.statement: Its skull is estimated to be 180 centimeters long, making it one of the largest known centrosaurine skulls.
facts.quote: Se estima que el cráneo mide 180 centímetros de largo, lo que lo convierte en uno de los cráneos centrosaurinos más grandes conocidos.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ZCDM V0010 was discovered in the Xingezhuang Formation of the Wangshi Group in Shandong, China, during the summer of 2008.
facts.quote: En el verano de 2008, se descubrió el holotipo ZCDM V0010 en la formación Xingezhuang del grupo Wangshi, Shandong, China.

facts.statement: The genus was described and named by paleontologist Xu Xing and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops fue descrito y nombrado por el paleontólogo Xu Xing y sus colegas, en 2010.

facts.statement: The genus name means "Chinese horned face," derived from the Latin word for China and Greek words for horn and face.
facts.quote: El nombre del género Sinoceratops significa "cara china con cuernos", y se deriva de la palabra Sino, que se refiere a China del latín Sina, el país donde fue descubierto, y las palabras griegas keras, κέρας que significan "cuerno", y ops, ωψ que significa "cara".

facts.statement: This discovery was significant as it represented the first known ceratopsid in China and possibly the only one in Asia.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento fue significativo, porque representó el primer ceratópsido conocido en China y posiblemente el único ceratópsido de Asia.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from river sediments deposited during the Late Cretaceous Campanian to Maastrichtian, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue colectado en sedimentos fluviales que se depositaron durante el Campaniano - Maastrichtiano del Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente 72 - 66 millones de años.

facts.statement: It was assigned to the subfamily Centrosaurinae as a basal member by Xu et al. in 2010 based on skull characteristics.
facts.quote: Sinoceratops fue asignado a la subfamilia Centrosaurinae, como miembro basal por Xu et al. en 2010 basado en características presentes en el cráneo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest this genus may represent a lineage that invaded Asia from North America via Beringia.
facts.quote: La implicación podría ser que este género representa un linaje que invadió Asia desde América del Norte a través de Beringia.

facts.statement: The time range for Sinoceratops is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It lived alongside the common hadrosaurid Shantungosaurus, the tyrannosaurid Zhuchengtyrannus, the leptoceratopsid Zhuchengceratops, and the large hadrosaurid Huaxiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Habitó con Shantungosaurus, un hadrosáurido muy común al que se le asignó la mayor parte del material, Zhuchengtyrannus, un tiranosáurido asiático relacionado con Tarbosaurus, Zhuchengceratops, un leptoceratópsido asiático, y Huaxiaosaurus, un posible individuo mayor de Shantungosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Turanoceratops is a valid ceratopsid, as its identification has recently been questioned.
facts.quote: El único otro ceratópsido asiático posible es Turanoceratops, pero recientemente se ha cuestionado su identificación como ceratópsido.

rejected.statement: Sinoceratops is one of the largest known centrosaurines and is significantly larger than other basal members of the group.
rejected.quote: Sinoceratops is also significant due to the fact it is one of the largest known centrosaurines, and is much larger than any other known basal members of this group.

rejected.quote: Inside this row of hornlets there is a series of low knobs on the top of the frill, which are not seen in any other horned dinosaur.
